items.title: Get email notifications when access to your AWS accounts changes
items.content_text: This article explains how to get a readable email the moment access changes on the AWS accounts you choose to monitor, covering both IAM Identity Center and local IAM. The solution fills the gap left by the lack of a native, account-aware notification for access changes, and it enriches each event so the alert is actionable rather than raw.

items.content_text: AgentCore Runtime runs each session in its own isolated microVM, lets the session continue on a new microVM, and gives you configurable lifecycles, persistent session storage and fast V2 snapshot cold starts.his article connects those capabilities across the docs so your agents checkpoint before maxLifetime, resume cleanly on V2 and after deploys, and follow a cold-start plan that fits your Region, with every step linked to AWS documentation.

items.title: Troubleshooting instance type changes and pipeline execution failures in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
items.content_text: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio (SMUS) projects often fail when they move from exploration to production-adjacent machine learning (ML) pipelines. Larger instance types and non-interactive runs expose unraised quotas, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) guardrails, stale compute references, and role mismatches. This article helps ML engineers and platform teams match each symptom to its root cause, confirm it, apply the fix, and check production readiness before the first run.

items.content_text: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now publishes OpenTelemetry metrics to Amazon CloudWatch for your node-based clusters, and each metric carries attributes you can filter and aggregate on with Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) expressions. ElastiCache now offers two monitoring modes. Standard monitoring, the existing experience, continues to publish CloudWatch Metrics (Classic) every 60 seconds and now also publishes a core set of OpenTelemetry metrics at the same interval at no additional charge.

items.content_text: Developers automating the AWS Identity Store often can't tell whether an AccessDeniedException is an IAM policy issue or a customer managed key failure. This article shows how to use the exception's Reason field to classify the root cause programmatically, route incidents to the right team, and reduce mean time to resolution.

items.title: S3 Inventory delivery fails with 'internal error' when the destination bucket's default encryption uses a bare KMS alias instead of a fully qualified ARN.
items.content_text: S3 Inventory reports never deliver and the console shows only a generic "internal error." That message is a catch-all. This article documents one specific, easily-missed cause, where every permission you'd check looks correct. However, the destination bucket's SSE-KMS default encryption references the KMS key by a bare alias / key ID instead of a fully qualified key ARN.

items.title: Prevent unintended Amazon RDS cluster replacement when Terraform reads a dynamic Availability Zone list
items.content_text: AWS Regions grow over time as new Availability Zones are added. If your Terraform configuration reads the Region’s Availability Zone list dynamically and passes it directly into a database resource, that growth can have an unexpected consequence: the next terraform apply can propose deleting and rebuilding your cluster. In this post, you learn why this happens, how to prevent it in your Terraform, and how to protect the data on independent layers even if a destructive change slips through.

items.content_text:
On Amazon MSK, a Kafka Streams application can rebalance at a regular interval even though no instance joined or left. These are usually probing rebalances.
This article covers where to get the client and broker logs on MSK, the log lines that confirm it, the defaults and lower bounds of probing.rebalance.interval.ms, acceptable.recovery.lag and max.warmup.replicas, why two of them must change together, and why the RebalanceInProgress metric does not answer this question.

items.title: Why transaction.timeout.ms shows 10000 instead of 60000 in a Kafka Streams EOS application
items.content_text:
With processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2, Kafka Streams overrides the producer transaction.timeout.ms to 10,000 ms (not the documented 60,000 ms) and commit.interval.ms to 100 ms. This article shows which values actually apply, why Streams changes them, how to confirm the effective values from the startup log, and
the two constraints when you override them: startup fails if transaction.timeout.ms is below commit.interval.ms, and the broker's transaction.max.timeout.ms is the upper bound.

items.content_text: api-change:sagemaker-featurestore-runtime: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store now supports the UpdateRecord API, enabling partial updates to individual feature values in an existing Online Store record without rewriting the entire record. This reduces write payloads and latency for high-frequency feature-level writes . api-change:mgn: AWS Transform for migrations adds a second network migration option - apply your source security posture to existing VPCs. Upload a source network file with firewall rules, tag the in-scope VPCs, and AWS Transform matches source subnets to them by CIDR and generates the security groups. api-change:appintegrations: This release adds a force parameter to DeleteApplication and a ConflictException to UpdateApplication, letting customers delete applications with existing associations in one call and get a clear error when an update conflicts with the application's current state. api-change:ec2: This release adds support to retain interruptible Capacity Reservations in an active state when all capacity is reclaimed. api-change:medialive: AWS Elemental MediaLive now supports AB forensic video watermarking api-change:mwaa: Enabled customers to clear optional S3 paths (plugins, requirements, and startup script) for their Amazon MWAA environments by accepting empty strings for the associated fields in UpdateEnvironment requests. api-change:bedrock-agentcore: Batch evaluation now supports up to 10 CloudWatch log groups per CloudWatchLogsSource api-change:odb: Adds the ListFlexComponents API for listing the flex components available for a given DB system shape. api-change:sagemaker: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store now supports the Standard V2 online store type, which enables feature-level writes to feature groups. You can select Standard V2 when creating a feature group, and update the storage type of an existing feature group via UpdateFeatureGroup.

items.content_text: Explore and use Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) like a file system with the new S3 PowerShell Drive. You can mount your S3 storage as a drive and navigate it with the same commands that are frequently used for local files: Set-Location, Get-ChildItem, Get-Content, Set-Content, and Remove-Item. Browse buckets and prefixes, read and write […]

items.title: Best Practices for Using Apache Iceberg v3 Tables in Amazon Redshift
items.content_text: Amazon Redshift now supports Apache Iceberg v3 tables, introducing default column values, row lineage tracking, and deletion vectors. These capabilities enable more efficient schema evolution, incremental data pipelines, and faster update/delete performance for data lake workloads. This article guides data engineers and database administrators through implementing, upgrading to, and optimizing Iceberg v3 tables in Amazon Redshift.

items.title: Intermittent session drops through a stateful firewall after enabling a second Local Gateway BGP peer on AWS Outposts
items.content_text: Diagnose and fix intermittent long-lived-session drops that appear when you enable a second Local Gateway BGP peer on AWS Outposts behind a stateful firewall. The cause is an asymmetric return path; the fix is a BGP AS-path prepend that preserves full stateful inspection.

items.title: Best Practices for Long-Term System Table Retention in Amazon Redshift with Amazon S3 Tables
items.content_text: Amazon Redshift system tables capture critical operational signals - query executed, every connection made, every workload pattern. Until recently, this data was retained for only 7 days in-cluster, making long-term observability, compliance auditing, and performance trend analysis difficult without custom workarounds. This article guides database administrators and data engineers through implementing and optimizing the new system table integration with Amazon S3 Tables for extended retention

items.title: Building a governed incident response agent fleet with AWS Agent Registry
items.content_text: AWS Agent Registry is now generally available, but most teams meet it mid-sprawl: dozens of agents and MCP tools scattered across accounts, with no shared inventory, no cross-team discovery, and no audit trail. This how-to walks operations teams through one concrete AIOps use case, governing an incident response fleet, from creating a gated registry and registering tools to catching shadow agents and discovering tools at runtime.

items.title: "Topic not present in metadata after 60000 ms" on Amazon MSK: it may be an authorization failure, not a missing topic
items.content_text: When a Kafka producer fails with TimeoutException: Topic ... not present in metadata after 60000 ms, most people check whether the topic exists or whether the network is broken. But this error also occurs when the topic exists and the cluster is healthy: on MSK clusters using IAM access control, a missing DESCRIBE permission on the topic surfaces as exactly this error. This article explains why the message is misleading, how to confirm the cause from broker logs, and how to fix the IAM policy.

items.title: Upgrading Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ 3.13 to 4.2 In-Place: A Practical Walkthrough
items.content_text: This article walks through the in-place major version upgrade from RabbitMQ 3.13 to 4.2 on Amazon MQ. It happens on the same broker resource with no separate data migration step — but the upgrade *will* be blocked if you skip the prep work, and RabbitMQ 4 has breaking changes that can require client or configuration updates. Most of the effort is in the steps before you press the button.

items.content_text: Most teams associate security testing with traditional web applications, overlooking that their analytics dashboards, data pipelines, and ML endpoints carry equally exploitable attack surfaces. This article demonstrates how AWS Continuum's capabilities map across these workload types with a complete implementation walkthrough of pen testing an embedded QuickSight application — helping practitioners secure their entire stack, not just their web tier.
